translations.literal: Zhou Chen
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chen

sentences.zh: 九年命開會通河。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was ordered to open the Huitong Canal.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Yongle reign, the court ordered him to reopen the Huitong Canal.

sentences.zh: 會通河者，元至元中，以壽張尹韓仲暉言，自東平安民山鑿河至臨清，引汶絕濟，屬之衛河，為轉漕道，名曰「會通」。

translations.literal: The Huitong Canal: in the Zhiyuan era of Yuan, on the advice of Shouzhang magistrate Han Zhonghui, a channel was cut from Anmin Mountain in Dongping to Linqing, drawing the Wen River across the Ji, joining it to the Wei River as a grain-transport route, named "Huitong."
translations.idiomatic: The Huitong Canal had been dug in the Yuan Zhiyuan period at the suggestion of Han Zhonghui, magistrate of Shouzhang: from Anmin Mountain in eastern Ping to Linqing, the Wen was led across the Ji and linked to the Wei as a transport channel for tribute grain, and the work was called "Huitong."

sentences.zh: 然岸狹水淺，不任重載，故終元世海運為多。

translations.literal: Yet the banks were narrow and the water shallow, unable to bear heavy loads, so throughout the Yuan sea transport remained predominant.
translations.idiomatic: But its banks were narrow and its water shallow, so it could not take heavy cargoes; sea transport therefore dominated for the whole Yuan period.

sentences.zh: 明初輸餉遼東、北平，亦專用海運。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ming, supplying provisions to Liaodong and Beiping also relied solely on sea transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Ming, grain for Liaodong and Beiping was likewise moved only by sea.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十四年，河決原武，絕安山湖，會通遂淤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Hongwu, the river burst at Yuanwu, cut off Anshan Lake, and the Huitong Canal silted up.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 24 (1391), the Yellow River broke at Yuanwu, severed Anshan Lake, and the Huitong Canal silted shut.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，建北京，河海兼運。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle, Beijing was built, and river and sea transport were used together.
translations.idiomatic: When Beijing was built at the start of the Yongle reign, both river and sea routes were used.

sentences.zh: 海運險遠多失亡，而河運則由江、淮達陽武，發山西、河南丁夫，陸免百七十里入衛河，歷八遞運所，民苦其勞。

translations.literal: Sea transport was perilous and distant with much loss, while river transport reached Yangwu from the Yangtze and Huai, mobilizing corvée laborers from Shanxi and Henan, portaging one hundred seventy li overland into the Wei River, passing eight relay depots—the people suffered from the toil.
translations.idiomatic: Sea transport was dangerous, distant, and prone to loss, whereas the river route ran from the Yangtze and Huai to Yangwu; corvée from Shanxi and Henan then hauled grain one hundred seventy li overland into the Wei, through eight relay depots—a burden the people found crushing.

sentences.zh: 至是濟寧州同知潘叔正上言：「舊會通河四百五十餘里，淤者乃三之一，浚之便。」

translations.literal: At this time Jining subprefectural vice magistrate Pan Shuzheng memorialized: "The old Huitong Canal is over four hundred fifty li; about one third is silted—dredging it would be advantageous."
translations.idiomatic: Then Pan Shuzheng, vice magistrate of Jining Prefecture, submitted: "The old Huitong Canal runs more than four hundred fifty li; roughly a third is silted up—dredging it would pay."

sentences.zh: 於是命禮及刑部侍郎金純、都督周長往治之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Li was ordered, together with Vice Minister of Justice Jin Chun and Regional Commander Zhou Chang, to go and repair it.
translations.idiomatic: The court then sent Li, Vice Minister of Justice Jin Chun, and Regional Commander Zhou Chang to take charge of the work.

sentences.zh: 禮以會通之源，必資汶水。

translations.literal: Li held that the source of the Huitong must rely on the Wen River.
translations.idiomatic: Li judged that the Huitong could not be restored without the Wen River as its source.

sentences.zh: 乃用汶上老人白英策，築堽城及戴村壩，橫亙五里，遏汶流，使無南入洸而北歸海。

translations.literal: He then adopted the plan of the old man of Wenshang, Bai Ying, building the Cheng city wall and the Daicun dam, stretching five li across, to check the Wen flow so it would not enter the Guang southward but return north to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the scheme of Bai Ying, an elder of Wenshang: dams at Cheng and Daicun, five li across, to hold the Wen so it would not spill south into the Guang but be driven north toward the sea.

sentences.zh: 匯諸泉之水，盡出汶上，至南旺，中分之為二道，南流接徐、沛者十之四，北流達臨清者十之六。

translations.literal: Gathering the waters of all springs, all issued above Wenshang; reaching Nanwang, the flow was divided in two—four tenths south to join Xu and Pei, six tenths north to reach Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered every spring into the Wen above Wenshang; at Nanwang the stream was split in two—four parts sent south toward Xu and Pei, six parts north to Linqing.

sentences.zh: 南旺地勢高，決其水，南北皆註，所謂水脊也。

translations.literal: Nanwang's terrain was high; releasing its water, both north and south received flow—what is called the water's ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Nanwang sits on high ground; once the water was released there, it fed both branches—the "backbone" of the whole system.

sentences.zh: 因相地置閘，以時蓄泄。

translations.literal: Accordingly, sluice gates were placed according to the terrain, storing and releasing water in season.
translations.idiomatic: Sluices were set according to the lie of the land to store and release water as needed.

sentences.zh: 自分水北至臨清，地降九十尺，置閘十有七，而達於衛；

translations.literal: From the divide north to Linqing, the land fell ninety chi; seventeen sluices were set, reaching the Wei;
translations.idiomatic: From the divide north to Linqing the land dropped ninety chi; seventeen locks were built to carry the channel to the Wei;

sentences.zh: 南至沽頭，地降百十有六尺，置閘二十有一，而達於淮。

translations.literal: south to Gutou, the land fell one hundred sixteen chi; twenty-one sluices were set, reaching the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: south to Gutou it fell one hundred sixteen chi more, with twenty-one locks, until the channel reached the Huai.

sentences.zh: 凡發山東及徐州、應天、鎮江民三十萬，蠲租一百一十萬石有奇，二十旬而工成。

translations.literal: In all, three hundred thousand people from Shandong, Xuzhou, Yingtian, and Zhenjiang were mobilized; grain rents remitted exceeded one million one hundred thousand shi; the work was completed in twenty ten-day periods.
translations.idiomatic: Some three hundred thousand laborers were drafted from Shandong, Xuzhou, Yingtian, and Zhenjiang; more than 1.1 million shi of tax grain was remitted; and the project was finished in two hundred days.

sentences.zh: 又奏浚沙河入馬常泊，以益汶。

translations.literal: He also memorialized dredging the Sha River into Machang Marsh to augment the Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He further proposed dredging the Sha River into Machang Marsh to swell the Wen.

sentences.zh: 語詳《河渠志》。

translations.literal: The details are given in the "Treatise on Rivers and Canals."
translations.idiomatic: The particulars are recorded in the Treatise on Rivers and Canals.

sentences.zh: 是年，帝復用工部侍郎張信言，使興安伯徐亨、工部侍郎蔣廷瓚會金純，浚祥符魚王口至中灤下，復舊黃河道，以殺水勢，使河不病漕，命禮兼董之。

translations.literal: That year, the emperor again followed Vice Minister of Works Zhang Xin's advice, sending Xing'an Earl Xu Heng and Vice Minister Jiang Tingzan to join Jin Chun in dredging from Xiangfu's Yuwang Mouth to below Zhongluan, restoring the old Yellow River course to reduce the water's force so the river would not harm transport—ordering Li to oversee it as well.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the emperor again took the counsel of Vice Minister Zhang Xin and sent Earl Xu Heng of Xing'an and Vice Minister Jiang Tingzan to work with Jin Chun dredging from Yuwang Mouth in Xiangfu to below Zhongluan, reopening the old Yellow River bed to tame the current so it would not threaten the grain route—Li was told to supervise this too.

sentences.zh: 八月還京師，論功第一，受上賞。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he returned to the capital; ranked first in merit, he received the highest reward.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital in the eighth month, was ranked first for merit, and received the highest honors.

sentences.zh: 潘叔正亦賜衣鈔。

translations.literal: Pan Shuzheng also received gifts of robes and paper money.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Shuzheng was likewise rewarded with robes and cash.

sentences.zh: 明年，以御史許堪言衛河水患，命禮往經畫。

translations.literal: The next year, on Censor Xu Kan's report of flooding on the Wei River, Li was ordered to go and plan remedies.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, after Censor Xu Kan reported flooding on the Wei, Li was sent to survey and plan relief.

sentences.zh: 禮請自魏家灣開支河二，泄水入土河，復自德州西北開支河一，泄水入舊黃河，使至海豐大沽河入海。

translations.literal: Li requested opening two branch channels from Weijia Bay to discharge water into the Tu River, and again one branch channel from northwest of Dezhou to discharge into the old Yellow River, reaching the sea via Haifeng and the Dagou River.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed two branches from Weijia Bay to spill into the Tu River, and another from northwest of Dezhou into the old Yellow River bed so floodwater could reach the sea through Haifeng and the Dagou.

sentences.zh: 帝命俟秋成後為之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that this wait until after the autumn harvest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told them to wait until after the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 禮還言：「海運經歷險阻，每歲船輒損敗，有漂沒者。

translations.literal: On his return Li said: "Sea transport passes through peril; every year ships are damaged, and some are lost at sea.
translations.idiomatic: On returning, Li reported: "The sea route is full of hazards; every year ships are damaged and some are lost outright.

sentences.zh: 有司修補，迫於期限，多科斂為民病，而船亦不堅。

translations.literal: Officials repair them under deadline pressure, levying heavily and harming the people, while the ships themselves are not sturdy.
translations.idiomatic: Officials rush repairs to meet deadlines, levy extra charges that burden the people, and the vessels themselves are poorly built.

sentences.zh: 計海船一艘，用百人而運千石，其費可辦河船容二百石者二十，船用十人，可運四千石。

translations.literal: Calculating: one sea ship uses one hundred men to move one thousand shi; the same cost could supply twenty river boats of two hundred shi each, ten men per boat, moving four thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: One seagoing vessel needs a hundred men to move a thousand shi; the same expense would fit out twenty river boats of two hundred shi each, ten men apiece, carrying four thousand shi in all.

sentences.zh: 以此而論，利病較然。

translations.literal: By this reckoning, benefit and harm are quite clear.
translations.idiomatic: On that basis the balance of advantage is obvious.

sentences.zh: 請撥鎮江、鳳陽、淮安、揚州及兗州糧，合百萬石，從河運給北京。

translations.literal: He requested allocating grain from Zhenjiang, Fengyang, Huai'an, Yangzhou, and Yanzhou—one million shi in all—to supply Beijing by river transport.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that grain from Zhenjiang, Fengyang, Huai'an, Yangzhou, and Yanzhou—one million shi altogether—be sent to Beijing by canal.

sentences.zh: 其海道則三歲兩運。」

translations.literal: The sea route would then run only twice in three years.
translations.idiomatic: The sea route could be used only twice every three years.

sentences.zh: 已而平江伯陳瑄治江、淮間諸河功，亦相繼告竣。

translations.literal: Soon after, Pingjiang Earl Chen Xuan's work on the rivers between the Yangtze and Huai was also reported complete in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Pingjiang Earl Chen Xuan likewise reported the Yangtze–Huai canal works finished.

sentences.zh: 於是河運大便利，漕粟益多。

translations.literal: Thereupon river transport became greatly convenient, and transported grain increased.
translations.idiomatic: River transport then became far easier, and ever more tribute grain moved by water.

sentences.zh: 十三年遂罷海運。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, sea transport was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year sea transport was ended altogether.

sentences.zh: 初，帝將營北京，命禮取材川蜀。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was about to build Beijing, he ordered Li to obtain timber from Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first planned Beijing, he sent Li to procure timber in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 禮伐山通道，奏言：「得大木數株，皆尋丈。

translations.literal: Li cut roads through the mountains and memorialized: "Several great trees were obtained, each several zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Li opened mountain passes and reported: "We felled several giants, each many zhang around.

sentences.zh: 一夕，自出谷中抵江上，聲如雷，不偃一草。」

translations.literal: In one night they came out of the valley themselves to the river, with a sound like thunder, not crushing a single blade of grass.
translations.idiomatic: In a single night they rolled from the valley to the river with a thunderous roar, yet not one blade of grass was bent.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以為瑞。

translations.literal: The court took this as an auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: The court hailed it as a portent of favor.

sentences.zh: 及河工成，復以采木入蜀。

translations.literal: When the canal work was finished, he was again sent into Sichuan to gather timber.
translations.idiomatic: After the canal was done he was again dispatched to Sichuan for timber.

sentences.zh: 十六年命治獄江西。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was ordered to handle judicial cases in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was assigned to review prisons in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 明年造番舟。

translations.literal: The next year he built foreign-trade ships.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he oversaw construction of ocean-going vessels.

sentences.zh: 自蜀召還，以老疾免朝參，有奏事令侍郎代。

translations.literal: Recalled from Sichuan, on account of age and illness he was excused from court attendance; when he had business to report, a vice minister was told to act for him.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from Sichuan, he was excused from daily audience because of age and illness; a vice minister stood in whenever he needed to memorialize.

sentences.zh: 二十年七月卒於官。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twentieth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the seventh month of the twentieth year.

sentences.zh: 禮性剛，馭下嚴急，故易集事，以是亦不為人所親。

translations.literal: Li's nature was stern; he governed subordinates with severity and urgency, so tasks were easily gathered—but for that reason he was not close to people.
translations.idiomatic: Li was hard by nature and drove his subordinates harshly, which made work move quickly but won him little affection.

sentences.zh: 卒之日，家無余財。

translations.literal: On the day he died, his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his household had nothing left.

sentences.zh: 洪熙改元，禮部尚書呂震請予葬祭如制。

translations.literal: At the Hongxi reign change, Minister of Rites Lü Zhen requested burial and sacrifices according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: At the Hongxi accession, Minister of Rites Lü Zhen asked that he receive the standard burial rites.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，主事王寵始請立祠。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi period, Director Wang Chong first requested establishing a shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi, Director Wang Chong first petitioned for a shrine.

sentences.zh: 詔祀之南旺湖上，以金純、周長配。

translations.literal: An edict ordered sacrifice at Nanwang Lake, with Jin Chun and Zhou Chang as associated spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered sacrifices at Nanwang Lake, with Jin Chun and Zhou Chang enshrined beside him.

sentences.zh: 隆慶六年贈禮太子太保。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Longqing he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 6 he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 藺芳，夏縣人。

translations.literal: Lin Fang, a native of Xia County.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Fang was a native of Xia County.

sentences.zh: 洪武中舉孝廉。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu period he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: During Hongwu he was nominated as Filial and Incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 累遷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He rose through promotions to Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，出為吉安知府。

translations.literal: In the Yongle period he went out as prefect of Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongle he was posted as prefect of Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 寬厚廉潔，民甚德之。

translations.literal: Generous, honest, and clean, the people greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Mild, honest, and frugal, the people held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 吉水民詣闕言縣有銀礦，遣使覆視。

translations.literal: People of Jishui went to court saying the county had silver mines; envoys were sent to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When people of Jishui petitioned the throne claiming a silver mine in the county, inspectors were dispatched to verify.

sentences.zh: 父老遮芳訴曰：「聞宋季嘗有言此者，卒以妄得罪。

translations.literal: Elders blocked Fang and pleaded: "We hear that in the Song season someone once said this and in the end was punished for falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: Village elders stopped Fang and pleaded: "We are told that in Song times someone made the same claim and was punished for a false report.

sentences.zh: 今皆樹藝地，安所得銀礦？」

translations.literal: Now all is planted land—where would silver mines come from?
translations.idiomatic: These fields are all under cultivation—where would any mine be?

sentences.zh: 芳詰告者，知其誣。

translations.literal: Fang interrogated the accusers and knew it was false.
translations.idiomatic: Fang questioned the petitioners and found the charge fabricated.

sentences.zh: 獄具，同官不敢署名，芳請獨任之。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, colleagues dared not sign; Fang asked to bear responsibility alone.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was ready, his colleagues refused to sign; Fang asked to take sole responsibility.

sentences.zh: 奏上，帝曰：「吾固知妄也。」

translations.literal: The memorial went up; the emperor said: "I already knew it was false.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached the throne; the emperor said, "I knew all along it was nonsense.

sentences.zh: 得寢。

translations.literal: The matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 已，坐事謫辦事官，從宋禮治會通河，復為工部都水主事。

translations.literal: Later, punished for an offense, he was demoted to a clerical officer, followed Song Li in repairing the Huitong Canal, and was restored as Director of Waterways in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after a disciplinary demotion, he served under Song Li on the Huitong Canal and was restored as director of waterways in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 十年，河決陽武，灌中牟、祥符、尉氏，遣芳按視。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the river burst at Yangwu, flooding Zhongmou, Xiangfu, and Weishi; Fang was sent to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Yellow River broke at Yangwu and inundated Zhongmou, Xiangfu, and Weishi; Fang was sent to survey the damage.

sentences.zh: 芳言：「中鹽堤當暴流之沖，請加築塞。」

translations.literal: Fang said: "The Zhongyan embankment faces the main rush of flood—please add height and blocking.
translations.idiomatic: Fang reported: "The Zhongyan levee lies in the path of the main flood—please raise and strengthen it.

sentences.zh: 又言：「自中灤分導河流，使由故道北入海，誠萬世利。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Diverting the river from Zhongluan so it follows the old course north to the sea would truly benefit ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged diverting the stream at Zhongluan into the old northern bed to the sea—a benefit for ages.

sentences.zh: 又言：「新築岸埽，止用草索，不能堅久。

translations.literal: He also said: "Newly built bank revetments use only straw ropes and cannot last.
translations.idiomatic: He further noted that new revetments tied only with straw could not endure.

sentences.zh: 宜編木成大囷，貫樁其中，實以瓦石，復以木橫貫樁表，牽築堤上，則殺水固堤之長策也。」

translations.literal: It would be better to weave timber into great bins, drive piles through them, fill with tile and stone, then run timbers horizontally through the pile tops and draw them onto the dike—then reducing water and securing the dike would be a lasting strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Timber should be woven into large cages, piles driven through them and packed with stone, then cross-timbers lashed atop and set into the levee—that, he said, was the sure way to tame the current and hold the bank.

sentences.zh: 詔悉從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 其後築堤者遵用其法。

translations.literal: Thereafter dike builders followed his method.
translations.idiomatic: Dike builders thereafter followed his method.

sentences.zh: 以宋禮薦，擢工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: On Song Li's recommendation, he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Song Li, he was promoted to vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 亡何，行太仆卿楊砥言：「吳橋、東光、興濟、交河及天津屯田，雨水決堤傷稼。

translations.literal: Before long, Acting Grand Master of Studs Yang Di said: "At Wuqiao, Dongguang, Xingji, Jiaohe, and Tianjin military colonies, rain broke dikes and harmed crops.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Acting Grand Master of Studs Yang Di reported that rains had breached dikes and ruined crops at Wuqiao, Dongguang, Xingji, Jiaohe, and the Tianjin garrison farms.

sentences.zh: 乞開德州良店東南黃河故道，以分水勢。」

translations.literal: He begged to open the old Yellow River course southeast of Liangdian in Dezhou to divide the water's force.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to reopen the old Yellow River channel southeast of Liangdian in Dezhou to split the flood.

sentences.zh: 復命芳往治之。

translations.literal: Fang was again ordered to go and repair it.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was again sent to handle the work.

sentences.zh: 所經郡邑，有不便民者輒疏以聞。

translations.literal: In every prefecture and county he passed, wherever something did not benefit the people he memorialized at once.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he found policies that harmed the people, he memorialized immediately.

sentences.zh: 事竣還。

translations.literal: When the work was done he returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the project was finished he returned.

sentences.zh: 十五年十一月卒於官。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifteenth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the eleventh month of the fifteenth year.

sentences.zh: 芳自奉約，布衣蔬食。

translations.literal: Fang kept his vows, wearing plain cloth and eating simple food.
translations.idiomatic: Fang lived plainly on coarse food and homespun cloth.

sentences.zh: 事母至孝。

translations.literal: He served his mother with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply filial toward his mother.

sentences.zh: 母甚賢。

translations.literal: His mother was very worthy.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was a woman of great judgment.

sentences.zh: 芳所治事，暮必告母。

translations.literal: Whatever Fang handled in office, each evening he told his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Each evening he reported the day's official business to her.

sentences.zh: 有不當，輒加教誡。

translations.literal: If anything was improper, she would admonish and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: When something was amiss, she corrected him at once.

sentences.zh: 芳受命唯謹，由是為良吏雲。

translations.literal: Fang received orders with sole care—thus he was called a good official.
translations.idiomatic: Fang obeyed her scrupulously and was reckoned a model magistrate.

sentences.zh: 陳瑄，字彥純，合肥人。

translations.literal: Chen Xuan, style Yanchun, a native of Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xuan, courtesy name Yanchun, was a native of Hefei.

sentences.zh: 父聞，以義兵千戶歸太祖，累官都指揮同知。

translations.literal: His father Wen, as a righteous-army chiliarch, submitted to the founding emperor and rose through offices to Vice Commissioner-in-chief of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wen had joined the founder as a chiliarch of volunteer troops and rose to vice commissioner-in-chief of the chief military commission.

sentences.zh: 瑄代父職。

translations.literal: Xuan succeeded to his father's post.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan inherited his father's post.

sentences.zh: 父坐事戍遼陽，瑄伏闕請代，詔並原其父子。

translations.literal: When his father was punished and exiled to guard Liaoyang, Xuan prostrated himself at the palace gate to beg to take his place; an edict pardoned both father and son.
translations.idiomatic: When his father was sentenced to garrison duty in Liaoyang, Xuan knelt at the palace gate offering to serve in his stead; the throne pardoned them both.

sentences.zh: 瑄少從大將軍幕，以射雁見稱。

translations.literal: In youth Xuan followed a great general's staff and was famed for shooting wild geese.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served on a field marshal's staff and was famed for bringing down wild geese with a bow.

sentences.zh: 屢從征南番，又征越巂，討建昌叛番月魯帖木兒，逾梁山，平天星寨，破寧番諸蠻。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed campaigns against southern barbarians, also campaigned in Yuexi, suppressed the Jianchang rebel barbarian Yue Lu Tiemuer, crossed Liang Mountain, pacified Tianxing Stockade, and broke the Ningfan barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned repeatedly in the south, in Yuexi, and against the Jianchang rebel Yue Lu Tiemuer; he crossed Liang Mountain, took Tianxing Stockade, and defeated the Ningfan tribes.

sentences.zh: 復征鹽井，進攻卜水瓦寨。

translations.literal: He again campaigned at Yanjing and advanced to attack Bushuiwa Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at Salt Wells and advanced on Bushuiwa Stockade.

sentences.zh: 賊熾甚。

translations.literal: The rebels were very fierce.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy was fierce.

sentences.zh: 瑄將中軍，賊圍之數重。

translations.literal: Xuan commanded the center army; the rebels surrounded him in many rings.
translations.idiomatic: Leading the center, Xuan was surrounded many times over.

sentences.zh: 瑄下馬射，傷足，裹創戰。

translations.literal: Xuan dismounted to shoot, was wounded in the foot, bound the wound and fought on.
translations.idiomatic: He dismounted to shoot, was wounded in the foot, bound the wound, and kept fighting.

sentences.zh: 自巳至酉，全師還。

translations.literal: From the si hour to the you hour, the whole army returned.
translations.idiomatic: From mid-morning until evening the whole force withdrew intact.

sentences.zh: 又從征賈哈剌，以奇兵涉打沖河，得間道，作浮梁渡軍。

translations.literal: Again following the campaign against Jia Halazi, with a surprise force he crossed the Dachong River, found a bypath, and built a pontoon bridge to ferry the army across.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned again against Jia Halazi, led a flanking force across the Dachong River by a hidden route, and threw a pontoon bridge across to carry the army over.

sentences.zh: 既渡，撤梁，示士卒不返，連戰破賊。

translations.literal: Once across, he removed the bridge, showing the troops there would be no return, and in successive battles broke the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: After the crossing he cut the bridge behind them to show there would be no retreat, then routed the enemy in a series of battles.

sentences.zh: 又會雲南兵征百夷有功，遷四川行都司都指揮同知。

translations.literal: Again joining Yunnan troops in campaigning against the Baiyi, he merited distinction and was transferred to Vice Commissioner-in-chief of the Sichuan Regional Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He then campaigned with Yunnan forces against the Baiyi tribes with distinction and was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief of the Sichuan regional chief military commission.

sentences.zh: 九年命與豐城侯李彬統浙、閩兵捕海寇。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was ordered, together with Marquis of Fengcheng Li Bin, to command Zhejiang and Fujian troops to capture sea pirates.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yongle he and Marquis of Fengcheng Li Bin were ordered to lead Zhejiang and Fujian forces against sea pirates.

sentences.zh: 海溢堤圮，自海門至鹽城凡百三十里。

translations.literal: The sea overflowed and the dikes collapsed; from Haimen to Yancheng the stretch totaled one hundred thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: When the sea burst its banks and the dikes collapsed, one hundred thirty li of coast from Haimen to Yancheng lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 命瑄以四十萬卒築治之，為捍潮堤萬八千余丈。

translations.literal: Xuan was ordered with four hundred thousand laborers to build and repair it, making tide-defending dikes of more than eighteen thousand zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was put in charge of four hundred thousand workers and built more than eighteen thousand zhang of seawalls against the tide.

sentences.zh: 明年，瑄言：「嘉定瀕海地，江流沖會。

translations.literal: The next year Xuan said: "Jiading lies on the coast; river currents converge there.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Xuan memorialized: "Jiading stands on the coast where river currents meet.

sentences.zh: 海舟停泊於此，無高山大陵可依。

translations.literal: Sea vessels moor here, yet there are no high mountains or great hills to rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: Ships put in here, but there are no mountains or hills to serve as landmarks.

sentences.zh: 請於青浦築土山，方百丈，高三十余丈，立堠表識。」

translations.literal: I request building an earthen hill at Qingpu, one hundred zhang square and more than thirty zhang high, and erecting a beacon to mark it."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that an earthen mound one hundred zhang square and over thirty zhang high be raised at Qingpu, with a beacon set up as a marker.

sentences.zh: 既成，賜名寶山，帝親為文記之。

translations.literal: Once completed, it was granted the name Baoshan, and the emperor personally composed an inscription for it.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished the hill was named Baoshan, and the emperor himself wrote an inscription commemorating it.

sentences.zh: 宋禮既治會通河成，朝廷議罷海運，仍以瑄董漕運。

translations.literal: When Song Li had finished repairing the Huitong Canal, the court debated abolishing sea transport and again put Xuan in charge of grain transport by canal.
translations.idiomatic: After Song Li completed the Huitong Canal, the court considered ending sea transport and again placed Xuan in charge of the grain-shipping system.

sentences.zh: 議造淺船二千余艘，初運二百萬石，浸至五百萬石，國用以饒。

translations.literal: It was proposed to build more than two thousand shallow-draft boats; the initial haul was two million shi, gradually reaching five million shi, and state revenue became abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Plans called for more than two thousand shallow-draft barges; shipments began at two million shi and eventually reached five million, and the treasury grew flush.

sentences.zh: 時江南漕舟抵淮安，率陸運過壩，逾淮達清河，勞費其鉅。

translations.literal: At that time when Jiangnan grain boats reached Huai'an, they generally went by land over the dam, crossed the Huai to reach Qinghe, and the labor and expense were enormous.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, grain barges from Jiangnan that reached Huai'an usually had to be hauled overland past the dam and across the Huai to Qinghe, at enormous labor and cost.

sentences.zh: 十三年，瑄用故老言，自淮安城西管家湖，鑿渠二十里，為清江浦，導湖水入淮，築四閘以時宣泄。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, following the advice of old hands, from west of Huai'an city at Guanjia Lake he dug a channel twenty li long, making the Qingjiang Sluice, guiding lake water into the Huai, and building four sluice gates to regulate discharge in season.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Yongle, acting on veterans' advice, he cut a twenty-li channel from Guanjia Lake west of Huai'an city to form the Qingjiang Sluice, fed lake water into the Huai, and built four gates to regulate the flow.

sentences.zh: 又緣湖十里築堤引舟，由是漕舟直達於河，省費不訾。

translations.literal: He also built dikes for ten li along the lake to lead boats, whereby grain boats went straight into the canal and expenses were cut beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: He also built ten li of dikes along the lake to guide shipping, so grain barges could reach the canal directly and costs fell immeasurably.

sentences.zh: 其後復浚徐州至濟寧河。

translations.literal: Later he again dredged the canal from Xuzhou to Jining.
translations.idiomatic: He later dredged the canal stretch from Xuzhou to Jining as well.

sentences.zh: 又以呂梁洪險惡，於西別鑿一渠，置二閘，蓄水通漕。

translations.literal: Because the Lüliang Rapids were perilous, he separately dug a channel to the west, set up two sluice gates, stored water, and opened the grain route.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Lüliang Rapids were treacherous, he cut a separate channel to the west, installed two sluice gates, impounded water, and kept the grain route open.

sentences.zh: 又築沛縣刁陽湖、濟寧南旺湖長堤，開泰州白塔河通大江。

translations.literal: He also built long dikes at Diaoyang Lake in Pei County and Nanwang Lake in Jining, and opened the Baita River in Taizhou to reach the great river.
translations.idiomatic: He also raised long dikes at Diaoyang Lake in Pei County and Nanwang Lake in Jining, and opened the Baita River in Taizhou to the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 又築高郵湖堤，於堤內鑿渠四十里，避風濤之險。

translations.literal: He also built dikes on Gaoyou Lake and dug a channel forty li within the dikes to avoid the peril of wind and waves.
translations.idiomatic: He also built dikes on Gaoyou Lake and cut a forty-li channel inside them to avoid the hazards of wind and waves.

sentences.zh: 又自淮至臨清，相水勢置閘四十有七，作常盈倉四十區於淮上，及徐州、臨清、通州皆置倉，便轉輸。

translations.literal: Again from the Huai to Linqing, according to water conditions he placed forty-seven sluice gates, made forty Changying granary districts on the Huai, and also placed granaries at Xuzhou, Linqing, and Tongzhou to facilitate transshipment.
translations.idiomatic: From the Huai to Linqing he placed forty-seven sluice gates according to the water, built forty Changying granary compounds on the Huai, and established granaries at Xuzhou, Linqing, and Tongzhou to ease transshipment.

sentences.zh: 慮漕舟膠淺，自淮至通州置舍五百六十八，舍置卒，導舟避淺。

translations.literal: Fearing grain boats would run aground in shallows, from the Huai to Tongzhou he placed five hundred sixty-eight stations, stationed soldiers at each station, and guided boats to avoid shallows.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing barges would ground in shallows, he set up five hundred sixty-eight way stations from the Huai to Tongzhou, garrisoned each with troops, and posted guides to steer boats clear of shoals.

sentences.zh: 復緣河堤鑿井樹木，以便行人。

translations.literal: He also dug wells and planted trees along the canal dikes to benefit travelers.
translations.idiomatic: He also sank wells and planted trees along the canal embankments for the convenience of travelers.

sentences.zh: 凡所規畫，精密宏遠，身理漕河者三十年，舉無遺策。

translations.literal: In all that he planned it was precise, vast, and far-reaching; for thirty years he personally managed the grain canal, and in everything there was no oversight.
translations.idiomatic: Everything he planned was meticulous and far-sighted; for thirty years he personally oversaw the grain canal, and nothing was left undone.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位之九月，瑄上疏陳七事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month after the Renzong emperor acceded, Xuan submitted a memorial setting forth seven matters.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month after the Renzong emperor's accession, Xuan submitted a memorial outlining seven proposals.

sentences.zh: 一曰南京國家根本，乞嚴守備。

translations.literal: First, Nanjing is the state's root; I beg that its defenses be strictly maintained.
translations.idiomatic: First, Nanjing is the foundation of the realm; I ask that its defenses be kept strict.

sentences.zh: 二曰推舉宜核實，無循資格，選朝臣公正者分巡天下。

translations.literal: Second, in promotion and recommendation verification should be solid; do not follow seniority alone, and select upright court officials to tour the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Second, promotions should be verified on merit rather than seniority alone, and upright court officials should be chosen to inspect the provinces.

sentences.zh: 三曰天下歲運糧餉，湖廣、江西、浙江及蘇、松諸府並去北京遠，往復逾年，上逋公租，下妨農事。

translations.literal: Third, the realm's annual transport of grain and supplies from Huguang, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, and the prefectures of Suzhou and Songjiang to Beijing is far; the round trip takes more than a year, delaying public rents above and hindering farming below.
translations.idiomatic: Third, the annual grain levy from Huguang, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, and Suzhou and Songjiang to Beijing is a long haul; the round trip takes more than a year, delaying tax payments and disrupting farming.

sentences.zh: 乞令轉至淮、徐等處，別令官軍接運至京。

translations.literal: I beg that it be transferred to places such as Huai'an and Xuzhou, and that separate official troops be ordered to carry it on to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that grain be delivered only as far as Huai'an and Xuzhou, with separate official convoys carrying it on to the capital.

sentences.zh: 又快船、馬船所載不過五六十石，每船官軍足用，有司添差軍民遞送，拘集聽候，至有凍餒，請革罷。

translations.literal: Again, fast boats and horse boats carry no more than fifty or sixty shi; the official troops on each boat are sufficient, yet the offices add conscripted soldiers and civilians for relay transport, summoning and waiting until some freeze or starve—I request that this be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Fast boats and horse barges carry no more than fifty or sixty shi and need no extra hands, yet officials keep drafting civilians for relay duty, keeping people waiting until some freeze or starve—I ask that this practice be ended.

sentences.zh: 四曰教職多非其人，乞考不職者黜之，選俊秀補生員，而軍中子弟亦令入學。

translations.literal: Fourth, many instructors are unfit for their posts; I beg that those who fail in office be dismissed, outstanding youths be chosen to fill student places, and sons of military households also be allowed to enter schools.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, many school instructors are unqualified; I ask that incompetent ones be removed, talented youths be enrolled as students, and sons of military households be allowed into the schools as well.

sentences.zh: 五曰軍伍竄亡，乞核其老疾者，以子弟代，逃亡者追補，戶絕者驗除。

translations.literal: Fifth, military households flee and hide; I beg that the aged and ill be verified, that sons and younger brothers replace them, fugitives be pursued and made up, and extinct households be checked and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, soldiers desert their registers; I ask that the aged and infirm be verified, sons and brothers take their place, deserters be hunted down and replaced, and extinct households struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 六曰開平等處，邊防要地，兵食虛乏，乞選練銳士，屯守兼務。

translations.literal: Sixth, at Kaiping and other places on the frontier, vital points lack troops and provisions; I beg that seasoned soldiers be chosen to garrison and farm at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, at Kaiping and other frontier posts troops and supplies run short; I ask that picked veterans be stationed there to garrison and farm together.

sentences.zh: 七曰漕運官軍，每歲北上，歸即修船，勤苦終年。

translations.literal: Seventh, grain-transport troops each year go north, and on returning immediately repair boats, toiling the whole year through.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, canal troops march north each year and, on returning, immediately repair their boats, laboring through the whole year.

sentences.zh: 該衛所又於其隙，雜役以重困之，乞加禁絕。

translations.literal: The responsible guard units also impose miscellaneous corvée duties in the intervals, heavily burdening them—I beg that this be strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Their guard units also pile on miscellaneous corvée duties in the intervals, crushing them further—I ask that this be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 帝覽奏曰：「瑄言皆當。」

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and said: "All of Xuan's words are apt."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and said, "Everything Xuan proposes is right.

sentences.zh: 令所司速行。

translations.literal: He ordered the relevant offices to execute them swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the responsible offices to act on it at once.

sentences.zh: 遂降敕獎諭，尋賜券，世襲平江伯。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict of commendation was issued, and soon he was granted a patent of nobility, inheriting the title Pingjiang Earl.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of praise followed, and soon he received a patent of nobility as hereditary Pingjiang Earl.

sentences.zh: 初，瑄以浚河有德於民，民立祠清河縣。

translations.literal: At first, because dredging the canal had benefited the people, the people established a shrine to him in Qinghe County.
translations.idiomatic: At first, because his canal work had benefited the people, they built him a shrine in Qinghe County.

sentences.zh: 正統中，命有司春秋致祭。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong era, the throne ordered the local offices to offer sacrifice in spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign the throne ordered local officials to offer sacrifices in spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 子銳嗣伯。

translations.literal: His son Rui succeeded to the earldom.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rui inherited the earldom.

sentences.zh: 成化初，分典三千營及團營。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chenghua reign he was put in charge of the Three Thousand Camp and the Tuan Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign he took command of the Three Thousand Camp and the Tuan Camp.

sentences.zh: 尋佩平蠻將軍印，總制兩廣。

translations.literal: Soon he wore the seal of General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and exercised overall command over the two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon received the seal of General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and took overall command of the two Guang.

sentences.zh: 移鎮淮陽，總督漕運。

translations.literal: He moved his headquarters to Huaiyang and served as grand coordinator of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He shifted his headquarters to Huaiyang and served as grand coordinator of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 建淮河口石閘及濟寧分水南北二閘。

translations.literal: He built stone sluice gates at the Huai River mouth and north-south dividing sluice gates at Jining.
translations.idiomatic: He built stone sluice gates at the mouth of the Huai and north-south dividing gates at Jining.

sentences.zh: 築堤疏泉，修舉廢墜。

translations.literal: He built dikes, cleared springs, and restored what had fallen into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: He raised dikes, cleared springs, and restored works that had fallen into decay.

sentences.zh: 總漕十四年，章數十上。

translations.literal: As grand coordinator of grain transport for fourteen years, he submitted dozens of memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Over fourteen years as grand coordinator of grain transport he submitted dozens of memorials.

sentences.zh: 日本貢使買民男女數人以歸，道淮安。

translations.literal: Japanese tribute envoys bought several men and women of the people and took them home, passing through Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese tribute envoys bought several commoners, men and women, and were taking them home when they passed through Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 銳留不遣，贖還其家。

translations.literal: Rui detained them and would not release them, ransoming them back to their families.
translations.idiomatic: Rui held them back, refused to let them go, and ransomed the captives back to their families.

sentences.zh: 淮、揚饑疫，煮糜施藥，多所存濟。

translations.literal: When Huai'an and Yangzhou suffered famine and pestilence, he boiled gruel and dispensed medicine, saving many lives.
translations.idiomatic: When famine and plague struck Huai'an and Yangzhou, he served porridge and distributed medicine and saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年，河決張秋，奉敕塞治。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongzhi the river burst at Zhangqiu, and by imperial order he blocked and repaired it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Hongzhi the river broke through at Zhangqiu, and by imperial order he sealed and repaired the breach.

sentences.zh: 還，增祿二百石，累加太傅兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: On returning, his stipend was increased by two hundred shi, and he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Tutor and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On his return his stipend was raised by two hundred shi, and he rose in stages to grand tutor and concurrently grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 十三年，火篩寇大同，銳以總兵官佩將軍印往援。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Huosai raided Datong, and Rui, as regional commander wearing the general's seal, went to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Hongzhi the Huosai raided Datong, and Rui went to the rescue as regional commander bearing the general's seal.

sentences.zh: 既至，擁兵自守，為給事中御史所劾，奪祿閑住。

translations.literal: Once there, he held his troops and merely defended himself; censors and investigating censors impeached him, and his stipend was taken and he was retired in idleness.
translations.idiomatic: Once there he kept his troops in camp and did nothing; supervising secretaries and censors impeached him, his stipend was cut, and he was sidelined.

sentences.zh: 其年卒。

translations.literal: That same year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the same year.

sentences.zh: 子熊嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xiong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 正德三年出督漕運。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengde he went out to supervise grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengde he was sent out to supervise grain transport.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾索金錢，熊不應，銜之。

translations.literal: Liu Jin demanded money; Xiong would not comply, and Jin bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin demanded a bribe; Xiong refused, and Jin nursed a grievance.

sentences.zh: 坐事，逮下詔獄，謫戍海南衛，奪誥券。

translations.literal: On a charge of misconduct he was arrested and sent to the imperial prison, banished to garrison Hainan Guard, and his patent of nobility was taken away.
translations.idiomatic: On a charge of misconduct he was thrown into the imperial prison, exiled to garrison duty at Hainan Guard, and stripped of his patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 熊故黷貨，在淮南頗殃民。

translations.literal: Xiong had long been corrupt in taking goods, and in Huainan he had greatly harmed the people.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong had long been venal, and in Huainan he had done the people considerable harm.

sentences.zh: 雖為瑾構陷，人無惜之者。

translations.literal: Although Jin had framed him, no one pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jin had framed him, no one mourned his fall.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，赦還復爵。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, Xiong was pardoned, returned, and restored to his title.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's execution he was pardoned, recalled, and restored to his title.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子。

translations.literal: He died without a son.
translations.idiomatic: He died without an heir.

sentences.zh: 再從子圭嗣。

translations.literal: His younger brother's son Gui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother's son Gui inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 以薦出鎮兩廣。

translations.literal: On recommendation he went out to command the two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he was sent out to command the two Guang.

sentences.zh: 封川寇起，圭督諸將往討，擒其魁，俘斬數千，加太子太保。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Fengchuan, Gui supervised the generals in an expedition, captured their leader, and killed or captured several thousand; he was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels rose in Fengchuan, Gui led the generals against them, seized their chief, and killed or captured several thousand; he was made grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 復平柳慶及賀連山賊，加太保，蔭一子。

translations.literal: He again pacified the bandits of Liuqing and Helianshan, was made Grand Tutor, and one son received hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the rebels of Liuqing and Helianshan as well, was made grand tutor, and one son received hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 安南範子儀等寇欽、廉，黎岐賊寇瓊厓，相掎角。

translations.literal: Fan Ziyi of Annam and others raided Qin and Lian, while the Li Qi bandits raided Qiongya, acting in mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ziyi of Annam and others raided Qin and Lian, while Li Qi's rebels struck Qiongya, coordinating their attacks.

sentences.zh: 圭移文安南，曉以利害，使縛子儀，而急出兵攻黎岐，敗走之。

translations.literal: Gui sent a dispatch to Annam, explaining advantage and harm, had them bind Fan Ziyi, and urgently sent troops to attack Li Qi and drive him off in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Gui wrote to Annam, explaining the stakes, had Fan Ziyi handed over, and then struck Li Qi hard and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 論功，復蔭一子，加歲祿四十石。

translations.literal: For merit he again granted hereditary privilege to one son and added forty shi to his annual stipend.
translations.idiomatic: For his service one more son received hereditary privilege and his annual stipend was raised by forty shi.

sentences.zh: 圭能與士卒同甘苦，聞賊所在，輒擐甲先登。

translations.literal: Gui could share hardship and comfort with soldiers; hearing where bandits were, he would don armor and be first to climb.
translations.idiomatic: Gui shared hardship with his men; whenever he heard where rebels were, he buckled on armor and led the climb.

sentences.zh: 深箐絕壑，沖冒瘴毒，無所避，以故所向克捷。

translations.literal: In deep ravines and sheer gorges he braved miasma and poison without avoidance, and for this reason wherever he went he achieved victory.
translations.idiomatic: In deep gorges and steep defiles he braved miasma without flinching, and for that reason he won wherever he fought.

sentences.zh: 在粵且十年，殲諸小賊不可勝數。

translations.literal: In Guangdong for nearly ten years, he destroyed countless small bandit bands.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly ten years in Guangdong he wiped out innumerable minor rebel bands.

sentences.zh: 召還，掌後軍府。

translations.literal: Recalled, he took charge of the Rear Army Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he took charge of the Rear Army Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 圭妻仇氏，鹹寧侯鸞女弟也。

translations.literal: Gui's wife was of the Qiu clan, the younger sister of Marquis of Xianning Luan.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was married to Lady Qiu, younger sister of Marquis of Xianning Luan.

sentences.zh: 圭深嫉鸞，鸞數短圭於世宗，幾得罪。

translations.literal: Gui deeply resented Luan; Luan repeatedly slandered Gui to the Shizong emperor, and Gui nearly came to grief.
translations.idiomatic: Gui deeply hated Luan, and Luan repeatedly maligned him to the Shizong emperor until he nearly fell.

sentences.zh: 鸞敗，帝益重圭，命總京營兵。

translations.literal: When Luan fell, the emperor valued Gui all the more and ordered him to command the capital camps.
translations.idiomatic: After Luan's downfall the emperor valued Gui all the more and put him in command of the capital garrisons.

sentences.zh: 寇入紫荊關，圭請出戰，營於盧溝，寇退而止。

translations.literal: When bandits entered Zijing Pass, Gui asked to go out and fight, encamped at Lugou, and stopped when the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders entered Zijing Pass, Gui asked to take the field, encamped at Lugou Bridge, and stood down when the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年，寇復入古北口，或議列營九門為備，圭以徒示弱無益，寇亦尋退。

translations.literal: The next year bandits again entered Gubeikou; some proposed lining camps at the Nine Gates as defense, but Gui held that this would only show weakness to no avail, and the bandits soon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The next year raiders entered Gubeikou again; some proposed deploying camps at the Nine Gates, but Gui argued that would only advertise weakness, and the raiders soon withdrew.

sentences.zh: 董築京師外城，加太子太傅。

translations.literal: He supervised construction of the outer wall of the capital and was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw construction of the capital's outer wall and was made grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太傅，謚武襄。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made grand tutor with the posthumous title Wuxiang.

sentences.zh: 子王謨嗣。

translations.literal: His son Wang Mo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Mo succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 僉書後軍，出鎮兩廣。

translations.literal: As vice minister of the Rear Army, he went out to command the two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: As vice minister of the Rear Army he was sent out to command the two Guang.

sentences.zh: 賊張璉反，屠掠數郡。

translations.literal: The bandit Zhang Lian rebelled and slaughtered and plundered several commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Zhang Lian rose in revolt and ravaged several prefectures.

sentences.zh: 王謨會提督張臬討平之，擒斬三萬余。

translations.literal: Wang Mo joined Grand Coordinator Zhang Tai in suppressing and pacifying them, capturing and killing more than thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mo joined Grand Coordinator Zhang Tai in crushing the revolt, capturing and killing more than thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 論功加太子太保，蔭一子。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and one son received hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made grand guardian of the heir apparent and one son received hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中出鎮淮安，總漕運，入掌前軍府事。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign he went out to command Huai'an, supervised grain transport, and entered to take charge of the Front Army Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign he was posted to Huai'an to supervise grain transport and later took charge of the Front Army Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈少保，謚武靖。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Junior Guardian and given the posthumous title Wujing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made junior guardian with the posthumous title Wujing.

sentences.zh: 傳至明亡，爵絕。

translations.literal: The line was transmitted until the Ming fell, and the title died out.
translations.idiomatic: The line continued until the dynasty's fall, when the title expired.

sentences.zh: 宣德八年進都指揮僉事，充左副總兵，代陳瑄鎮淮安，董漕運，累進左軍都督僉事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xuande he was promoted to Vice Commissioner-in-chief, served as Left Vice Commander-in-chief, replaced Chen Xuan in garrisoning Huai'an, supervised grain transport, and was repeatedly promoted to Left Regional Commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Xuande he rose to vice commissioner-in-chief, served as left vice commander-in-chief, replaced Chen Xuan at Huai'an to supervise grain transport, and was promoted in stages to left regional commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 淮安，瑜故鄉也，人以為榮。

translations.literal: Huai'an was Yu's native place, and people regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'an was Yu's hometown, and locals took pride in it.

sentences.zh: 在淮數年，守瑄成法不變，有善政。

translations.literal: For several years at Huai'an he kept Xuan's established methods unchanged and had good policies.
translations.idiomatic: For several years at Huai'an he kept Xuan's methods intact and governed well.

sentences.zh: 民有親在與弟訟產者。

translations.literal: There was a man with a living parent who sued his younger brother over property.
translations.idiomatic: One man still had a living parent yet sued his younger brother over an inheritance.

sentences.zh: 瑜曰：「訟弟不友，無親不孝。」

translations.literal: Yu said: "To sue one's younger brother is unfriendly; to have no parent is unfilial."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "Suing your brother shows no brotherly love; having no parent shows no filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 杖而斥之。

translations.literal: He had them beaten with rods and driven away.
translations.idiomatic: He had them beaten with rods and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 又有負金不能償，至翁婿兄弟相訟者。

translations.literal: There were also cases where men unable to repay gold went so far as to sue one another as father-in-law, son-in-law, and brothers.
translations.idiomatic: There were also cases in which men who could not repay debts sued one another across generations—as fathers-in-law, sons-in-law, and brothers.

sentences.zh: 瑜曰：「奈何以財故傷恩！」

translations.literal: Yu said: "How can one wound affection because of wealth!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "How can you let money destroy family ties!

sentences.zh: 即代償，勸其敦睦。

translations.literal: He immediately paid on their behalf and urged them to restore harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He paid the debt himself and urged them to live in harmony.

sentences.zh: 二卒盜敗舟一板，有司以盜官物，坐卒死。

translations.literal: Two soldiers stole one plank from a broken boat; the offices treated it as theft of government property and sentenced the soldiers to death.
translations.idiomatic: Two soldiers stole a single plank from a broken boat; the authorities treated it as theft of government property and sentenced them to death.

sentences.zh: 瑜曰：「兩卒之命，抵敗舟一板耶？」

translations.literal: Yu said: "Are the lives of two soldiers worth one plank from a broken boat?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "Are two soldiers' lives worth one plank from a wrecked boat?

sentences.zh: 竟得末減。

translations.literal: In the end they received reduced sentences.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the sentence was reduced to the lowest penalty.

sentences.zh: 歲兇，發官廩以振。

translations.literal: In years of famine, he released government granary stores to give relief.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years he opened government granaries to provide relief.

sentences.zh: 然性好貨，為英宗切責，而前所發不軌事有枉者。

translations.literal: Yet his nature loved goods; the Yingzong Emperor sharply rebuked him, and among the sedition cases he had previously exposed, some were wrongfully judged.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was greedy by nature; the Yingzong Emperor sharply rebuked him, and some of the sedition cases he had earlier brought forward had been wrongly prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 正統四年，議事入京。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengtong, he went to the capital to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhengtong he went to the capital for consultations.

sentences.zh: 得疾，束兩手如高懸狀，號救求解而卒。

translations.literal: He fell ill, bound his two hands as if hanging high, cried out begging to be released, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill, clasped his hands as though suspended from above, cried out for release, and died.

sentences.zh: 周忱，字恂如，吉水人。

translations.literal: Zhou Chen, styled Xunru, was a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chen, styled Xunru, came from Jishui.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the second year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士。

translations.literal: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He was chosen for the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 明年，成祖擇其中二十八人，令進學文淵閣。

translations.literal: The next year, the Chengzu Emperor chose twenty-eight of them and ordered them to study at the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Chengzu Emperor chose twenty-eight of them for advanced study at the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 忱自陳年少乞預。

translations.literal: Chen himself stated that he was young and begged to be included.
translations.idiomatic: Chen pleaded that, though young, he wished to join them.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其有誌，許之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his ambition and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his ambition and agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋擢刑部主事，進員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Punishments and advanced to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Punishments and then to vice director.

sentences.zh: 忱有經世才，浮沈郎署二十年，人無知者，獨夏原吉奇之。

translations.literal: Chen had talent for governing the age; he drifted in a secretary's post for twenty years with no one knowing him, only Xia Yuanji regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Chen had genuine statecraft talent, yet he spent twenty years unnoticed in a junior ministry post; only Xia Yuanji recognized his gifts.

sentences.zh: 洪熙改元，稍遷越府長史。

translations.literal: When the Hongxi reign title was adopted, he was slightly promoted to Chief Secretary of Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the Hongxi reign began, he was promoted to chief secretary of Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，有薦為郡守者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuande, someone recommended him as a prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuande reign someone recommended him for a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 原吉曰：「此常調也，安足盡周君？」

translations.literal: Yuan Ji said: "This is a routine assignment—how could it fully employ Master Zhou?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ji said, "That is a routine posting—how could it fully use Zhou's abilities?"

sentences.zh: 五年九月，帝以天下財賦多不理，而江南為甚，蘇州一郡，積逋至八百萬石，思得才力重臣往厘之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year, because fiscal revenue throughout the empire was largely mismanaged, and Jiangnan especially so—with Suzhou Prefecture alone owing eight million shi in arrears—the emperor sought a talented, high-ranking minister to go set it right.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fifth year, seeing that revenues nationwide were largely mishandled and Jiangnan worst of all—Suzhou Prefecture alone owed eight million shi in arrears—the emperor sought a capable senior minister to restore order.

sentences.zh: 乃用大學士楊榮薦，遷忱工部右侍郎，巡撫江南諸府，總督稅糧。

translations.literal: Thereupon, on Grand Secretary Yang Rong's recommendation, Chen was transferred to Right Vice Minister of Works, made touring pacification commissioner of the Jiangnan prefectures, and put in overall charge of tax grain.
translations.idiomatic: On Grand Secretary Yang Rong's recommendation he was made right vice minister of works, pacification commissioner for the Jiangnan prefectures, and chief overseer of tax grain.

sentences.zh: 始至，召父老問逋稅故。

translations.literal: When he first arrived, he summoned elders and asked the reasons for tax arrears.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he summoned local elders to learn why taxes fell into arrears.

sentences.zh: 皆言豪戶不肯加耗，並征之細民，民貧逃亡，而稅額益缺。

translations.literal: All said that great households refused to pay surcharges, which were levied together on common people; the people, poor, fled, and the tax quota grew ever shorter.
translations.idiomatic: They all said wealthy households refused to bear surcharge losses, so the burden fell on common taxpayers; the poor fled, and shortfalls grew worse.

sentences.zh: 忱乃創為平米法，令出耗必均。

translations.literal: Chen then created the pingmi method, ordering that outgoing surcharges must be equalized.
translations.idiomatic: Chen devised the equalized-surcharge method, requiring that handling-loss surcharges be spread evenly.

sentences.zh: 又請敕工部頒鐵斛，下諸縣準式，革糧長之大入小出者。

translations.literal: He also requested an imperial order for the Ministry of Works to issue iron bushels to all counties as standard measure, abolishing grain chiefs' practice of taking much and giving little.
translations.idiomatic: He also obtained an imperial order for iron bushels as the standard measure in every county, ending grain chiefs' practice of taking full measure in and giving short measure out.

sentences.zh: 舊例，糧長正副三人，以七月赴南京戶部領勘合。

translations.literal: Under the old rule, three grain chiefs—principal and deputies—went in the seventh month to the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue to receive verification documents.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system three grain chiefs, principal and deputies, traveled each seventh month to the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue for verification slips.

sentences.zh: 既畢，復賫送部。

translations.literal: When finished, they again conveyed them back to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: When done, they had to carry them back to the ministry again.

sentences.zh: 往反資費，皆科斂充之。

translations.literal: The round-trip expenses were all collected by levy to cover them.
translations.idiomatic: Round-trip costs were covered by levies on the people.

sentences.zh: 忱止設正副各一人，循環赴領。

translations.literal: Chen limited the posts to one principal and one deputy each, who went in rotation to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Chen reduced each county to one principal and one deputy grain chief, who took turns collecting the documents.

sentences.zh: 訖事，有司類收上之部。

translations.literal: When the matter was finished, the local offices collected them by category and sent them up to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: When the season ended, local offices collected the slips by category and forwarded them to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 民大便。

translations.literal: The people were greatly relieved.
translations.idiomatic: The people found the change a great relief.

sentences.zh: 忱見諸縣收糧無團局，糧長即家貯之，曰：「此致逋之由也。」

translations.literal: Chen saw that in the counties there were no centralized collection offices for grain; grain chiefs stored it at home, and said: "This is what causes arrears."
translations.idiomatic: Chen saw that counties had no centralized grain offices and that grain chiefs stored grain at home; he said, "That is what creates arrears."

sentences.zh: 遂令諸縣於水次置囤，囤設糧頭、囤戶各一人，名「轄收」。

translations.literal: He then ordered all counties to set up depots at waterside, each depot with one grain head and one depot keeper, called "sub-collection."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered each county to establish waterside depots, each with one grain head and one depot keeper—a system called "sub-collection."

sentences.zh: 至六七萬石以上，始立糧長一人總之，名「總收」。

translations.literal: Where the amount reached sixty or seventy thousand shi and above, one grain chief was established to oversee it all, called "aggregate collection."
translations.idiomatic: Where collections reached sixty or seventy thousand shi, one grain chief was appointed to oversee them—the "aggregate collection" system.

sentences.zh: 民持貼赴囤，官為監納，糧長但奉期會而已。

translations.literal: The people brought their receipts to the depot; officials supervised the payment; grain chiefs had only to meet the schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Taxpayers brought receipts to the depot under official supervision; grain chiefs need only meet their deadlines.

sentences.zh: 置撥運、綱運二簿。

translations.literal: He established two ledgers: allocation transport and convoy transport.
translations.idiomatic: He set up two ledgers—allocation transport and convoy transport.

sentences.zh: 撥運記支撥起運之數，預計所運京師、通州諸倉耗，以次定支。

translations.literal: Allocation transport recorded the numbers for disbursement and dispatch, estimating in advance the loss on grain shipped to the capital, Tongzhou, and other granaries, and fixing disbursements accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The allocation ledger recorded dispatch quotas and estimated shipping losses to the capital, Tongzhou, and other granaries, setting disbursements in proper order.

sentences.zh: 綱運聽其填註剝淺諸費，歸以償之。

translations.literal: Convoy transport allowed them to enter shallow-draft and other fees, which were repaid on return.
translations.idiomatic: The convoy ledger recorded shallow-draft and other transport fees for reimbursement on return.

sentences.zh: 支撥羨余，存貯在倉，曰「余米」。

translations.literal: Surplus from disbursement was stored in the granary and called "surplus grain."
translations.idiomatic: Disbursement surpluses were stored in granaries as "surplus grain."

sentences.zh: 次年余多則加六征，又次年加五征。

translations.literal: In the next year, if surplus was ample, a sixth-round levy was added; the year after, a fifth-round levy.
translations.idiomatic: If surplus was ample the next year, a sixth-round levy was added; the year after that, a fifth-round levy.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖平吳，盡籍其功臣子弟莊田入官，後惡富民豪並，坐罪沒入田產，皆謂之官田。

translations.literal: At first, when the Taizu Emperor pacified Wu, he registered all the estate fields of meritorious ministers' sons and younger brothers as government property; later, disliking the rich who monopolized wealth, he confiscated land by criminal conviction—all called government land.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu Emperor pacified Wu he registered the estate lands of meritorious families as government property; later, prosecuting wealthy monopolists, he confiscated their lands—all counted as government land.

sentences.zh: 按其家租籍征之，故蘇賦比他府獨重。

translations.literal: Tax was levied according to their household rent registers, so Suzhou's levy was uniquely heavy compared with other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Rent was assessed from household registers, which is why Suzhou's levies far exceeded other prefectures'.

sentences.zh: 官民田租共二百七十七萬石，而官田之租乃至二百六十二萬石，民不能堪。

translations.literal: Government and private land rents together totaled 2.77 million shi, yet government land rent alone reached 2.62 million shi; the people could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Official and private rents together totaled 2.77 million shi, but government-land rent alone came to 2.62 million shi—the people could not endure it.

sentences.zh: 時宣宗屢下詔減官田租，忱乃與知府況鍾曲算累月，減至七十二萬余石，他府以次減，民始少蘇。

translations.literal: At that time the Xuanzong Emperor repeatedly issued edicts reducing government land rent; Chen then with Prefect Kuang Zhong calculated minutely for months, reducing it to a little over 720,000 shi; other prefectures were reduced in turn, and the people slightly recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanzong Emperor had repeatedly ordered reductions in government-land rent; Chen and Prefect Kuang Zhong calculated for months and cut Suzhou's to just over 720,000 shi; other prefectures followed, and the people breathed easier.

sentences.zh: 七年，江南大稔，詔令諸府縣以官鈔平糴備振貸，蘇州遂得米二十九萬石。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Jiangnan had a great harvest; an edict ordered all prefectures and counties to buy grain at fair price with government notes to prepare for relief loans; Suzhou thereby obtained 290,000 shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Jiangnan enjoyed a bumper harvest; the court ordered prefectures and counties to buy grain at fair price with government notes against famine loans, and Suzhou secured 290,000 shi.

sentences.zh: 故時公侯祿米、軍官月俸皆支於南戶部。

translations.literal: Formerly, stipend grain for nobles and monthly pay for military officers were all disbursed by the southern Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly nobles' stipend grain and officers' monthly rations were all paid through the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 蘇、松民轉輸南京者，石加費六斗。

translations.literal: For the people of Suzhou and Songjiang who transported grain to Nanjing, six dou per shi was added as expense.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou and Songjiang taxpayers who shipped grain to Nanjing paid six dou per shi in transport costs.

sentences.zh: 忱奏令就各府支給，與船價米一斗，所余五斗，通計米四十萬石有奇，並官鈔所糴，共得米七十萬余石，遂置倉貯之，名曰「濟農」。

translations.literal: Chen memorialized ordering payment at each prefecture instead, giving one dou per shi for boat price; the remaining five dou, totaling a little over 400,000 shi of grain, together with grain bought with government notes, came to a little over 700,000 shi; he then established a granary to store it, named "Farm Relief."
translations.idiomatic: Chen obtained permission to pay stipends locally, keeping one dou per shi for shipping costs; the five dou saved on each shi totaled over 400,000 shi, which with government-note purchases brought the store to over 700,000 shi; he established a granary called the Farm Relief Granary.

sentences.zh: 振貸之外，歲有余羨。

translations.literal: Beyond relief loans, each year there was surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond famine relief and seed loans, the granary had a yearly surplus.

sentences.zh: 凡綱運、風漂、盜奪者，皆借給於此，秋成，抵數還官。

translations.literal: All convoy transport, storm losses, and theft were lent from here; at autumn harvest the amount was repaid to the government.
translations.idiomatic: Losses from convoy duty, storms, and theft were covered from this store and repaid after the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 其修圩、築岸、開河、浚湖所支口糧，不責償。

translations.literal: Ration grain dispensed for repairing dikes, building embankments, opening canals, and dredging lakes was not required to be repaid.
translations.idiomatic: Grain spent on dikes, embankments, canals, and lake dredging need not be repaid.

sentences.zh: 耕者借貸，必驗中下事力及田多寡給之，秋與糧並賦，兇歲再振。

translations.literal: For farmers who borrowed, verification of middle and lower productive capacity and the amount of land was required before granting; in autumn it was levied together with grain tax; in famine years relief was given again.
translations.idiomatic: Seed loans went only to farmers of moderate or lower means, scaled to their holdings; repayment came with the autumn grain tax, with additional relief in famine years.

sentences.zh: 其奸頑不償者，後不復給。

translations.literal: Those who were deceitful and stubborn and did not repay were not given loans again.
translations.idiomatic: Defaulters who proved dishonest received no further loans.

sentences.zh: 定為條約以聞。

translations.literal: He fixed regulations and reported them.
translations.idiomatic: He codified the rules and submitted them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉獎之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 終忱在任，江南數大郡，小民不知兇荒，兩稅未嘗逋負，忱之力也。

translations.literal: Throughout Chen's tenure, in several great prefectures of Jiangnan, common people did not know famine; the two taxes were never in arrears—this was Chen's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout Chen's tenure the common people of Jiangnan's great prefectures scarcely knew famine, and the land tax never fell into arrears—his work.

sentences.zh: 時漕運，軍民相半。

translations.literal: At that time for grain transport, military and civilian bore half each.
translations.idiomatic: Grain transport at the time split the burden evenly between military convoys and civilian labor.

sentences.zh: 軍船給之官，民則僦舟，加以雜耗，率三石致一石，往復經年失農業。

translations.literal: Military ships were supplied by the government; civilians rented boats, with miscellaneous losses added—generally three shi to deliver one shi; going and returning took a year, losing agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Military convoys used government ships; civilians hired boats and paid heavy surcharges—often three shi to deliver one—and a round trip cost a full year's farming.

sentences.zh: 忱與平江伯陳瑄議，民運至淮安或瓜洲水次交兌，漕軍運抵通州。

translations.literal: Chen and the Marquis of Pingjiang, Chen Xuan, discussed having civilians transport to Huai'an or Guazhou waterside for exchange delivery, and transport troops carry to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen and Marquis Chen Xuan of Pingjiang devised exchange delivery: civilians would haul grain to Huai'an or Guazhou, and transport troops would carry it on to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 淮安石加五斗，瓜洲又益五升。

translations.literal: At Huai'an five dou per shi was added; at Guazhou another five sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shippers received five dou per shi at Huai'an and an additional five sheng at Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 其附近並南京軍未過江者，即倉交兌，加與過江米二斗。

translations.literal: For those nearby and for Nanjing troops who had not crossed the river, exchange was at the granary, with two dou of cross-river grain added.
translations.idiomatic: Nearby districts and Nanjing garrisons that did not cross the Yangtze exchanged at local granaries, with two dou per shi added for the river crossing.

sentences.zh: 襯墊蘆席，與折米五合。

translations.literal: Padding mats and reed screens were compensated with grain converted at five he.
translations.idiomatic: Padding mats and reed screens were compensated at five he of grain per shi.

sentences.zh: 兌軍或後期阻風，則令州縣支贏米。

translations.literal: If transport troops were late or blocked by wind, prefectures and counties were ordered to disburse surplus grain.
translations.idiomatic: When convoy troops were delayed by wind, local officials supplied surplus grain from store.

sentences.zh: 設廒於瓜洲水次，遷米貯之，量支余米給守者。

translations.literal: Granaries were set up at Guazhou waterside; grain was moved and stored there, and surplus grain was measured out to pay the guards.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries at Guazhou stored transferred grain, and surplus grain paid the guards.

sentences.zh: 由是漕費大省。

translations.literal: From this, grain transport costs were greatly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Transport costs fell sharply.

sentences.zh: 民間馬草歲運兩京，勞費不訾。

translations.literal: Among the people, horse fodder was transported yearly to both capitals; the labor and expense were incalculable.
translations.idiomatic: Civilian transport of horse fodder to both capitals each year was ruinously costly.

sentences.zh: 忱請每束折銀三分，南京則輕賫即地買納。

translations.literal: Chen requested that each bundle be converted to three fen of silver; for Nanjing, light delivery and local purchase and payment.
translations.idiomatic: Chen proposed converting each bundle to three fen of silver; in Nanjing fodder could be bought and delivered locally.

sentences.zh: 京師百官月俸，皆持俸帖赴領南京。

translations.literal: Monthly salaries of all officials in the capital were all received at Nanjing by presenting salary slips.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials collected monthly salaries in Nanjing with pay vouchers.

sentences.zh: 米賤時，俸貼七八石，僅易銀一兩。

translations.literal: When grain was cheap, salary slips of seven or eight shi traded for only one liang of silver.
translations.idiomatic: When grain was cheap, a voucher for seven or eight shi fetched only one tael of silver.

sentences.zh: 忱請檢重額官田、極貧下戶兩稅，準折納金花銀，每兩當米四石，解京兌俸，民出甚少，而官俸常足。

translations.literal: Chen requested selecting heavy-quota government land and the poorest households' two taxes, converting to patterned-silver payment at four shi per liang, remitting to the capital to redeem salaries; the people paid very little, yet official salaries were always sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Chen arranged for households on heavy government land and the poorest taxpayers to pay silver-in-lieu at four shi per tael, remitted to the capital for salaries—fewer burdens on the people, full pay for officials.

sentences.zh: 嘉定、昆山諸縣歲納布，疋重三斤抵糧一石。

translations.literal: Jiading, Kunshan, and other counties paid cloth yearly; each bolt weighing three jin counted as one shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Jiading, Kunshan, and other counties paid tax in cloth, one bolt of three jin counting as one shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 比解，以縷粗見斥者十八九。

translations.literal: When presented, eight or nine out of ten were rejected for coarse thread.
translations.idiomatic: At delivery, eight or nine bolts in ten were rejected for coarse weaving.

sentences.zh: 忱言：「布縷細必輕，然價益高。

translations.literal: Chen said: "Fine thread in cloth must be light, yet the price rises higher.
translations.idiomatic: Chen argued, "Fine thread makes lighter cloth, but the price rises accordingly.

sentences.zh: 今既貴重，勢不容細。

translations.literal: Now that it is costly and heavy, fineness cannot be demanded.
translations.idiomatic: Now that cloth is costly, fineness cannot be demanded.

sentences.zh: 乞自今不拘輕重，務取長廣如式。」

translations.literal: I beg that from now on weight not be fixed—only that length and width meet the standard."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that hereafter weight be ignored so long as length and width meet the standard."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 各郡驛馬及一切供帳，舊皆領於馬頭。

translations.literal: In each prefecture, relay horses and all provisioning were formerly managed by horse heads.
translations.idiomatic: Relay horses and all travel supplies had been managed by relay station chiefs.
