sentences.zh: 有耗損，則馬頭橫科補買。

translations.literal: When there was loss, horse heads levied arbitrarily to make up purchases.
translations.idiomatic: Losses were made up by arbitrary levies on the people.

sentences.zh: 忱令田畝出米升九合，與秋糧俱征，驗馬上中下直給米。

translations.literal: Chen ordered nine he of grain per mu of field, levied together with autumn grain; horses were inspected as upper, middle, or lower grade and paid grain accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Chen levied nine he of grain per mu with the autumn tax and paid relay stations grain according to each horse's grade.

sentences.zh: 正統初，淮、揚災，鹽課虧，敕忱巡視。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengtong, Huai and Yang suffered disaster; salt revenue fell short; Chen was ordered to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengtong, disasters struck Huai and Yang and salt revenues fell short; Chen was ordered to inspect.

sentences.zh: 奏令蘇州諸府，撥余米一二萬石連揚州鹽場，聽抵明年田租，竈戶得納鹽給米。

translations.literal: He memorialized ordering Suzhou and other prefectures to allocate ten or twenty thousand shi of surplus grain to Yangzhou salt works, allowing offset against next year's land tax; salt producers could pay salt and receive grain.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged for Suzhou and other prefectures to send ten or twenty thousand shi of surplus grain to Yangzhou salt works, deductible against the next year's land tax, so salters could deliver salt and receive grain.

sentences.zh: 時米貴鹽賤，官得積鹽，民得食米，公私大濟。

translations.literal: At the time grain was dear and salt cheap; the government obtained accumulated salt, the people obtained food grain—both public and private were greatly helped.
translations.idiomatic: With grain dear and salt cheap, the state built salt reserves while the people got grain—a great boon to public and private interests alike.

sentences.zh: 尋敕兼理松江鹽課。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered also to manage Songjiang salt revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon put in charge of Songjiang salt revenues as well.

sentences.zh: 華亭、上海二縣逋課至六十三萬余引，竈丁逃亡。

translations.literal: Huating and Shanghai two counties owed over 630,000 yin in arrears; salt workers fled.
translations.idiomatic: Huating and Shanghai owed over 630,000 yin in arrears, and salters had fled.

sentences.zh: 忱謂田賦宜養農夫，鹽課宜養竈丁。

translations.literal: Chen said land tax should nourish farmers, salt revenue should nourish salt workers.
translations.idiomatic: Chen held that land tax should sustain farmers and salt revenue should sustain salters.

sentences.zh: 因上便宜四事，命速行之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted four expedient measures and was ordered to implement them quickly.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted four practical measures and was ordered to implement them at once.

sentences.zh: 忱為節竈戶運耗，得米三萬二千余石。

translations.literal: Chen, to economize transport loss for salt households, obtained over 32,000 shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: By cutting salters' transport losses, Chen saved over 32,000 shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 亦仿濟農倉法，置贍鹽倉，益補逃亡缺額。

translations.literal: He also, following the Farm Relief Granary method, established a Salt Sustenance Granary, further making up shortfalls from those who fled.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Farm Relief Granary model, he established a Salt Sustenance Granary to cover shortfalls left by fugitive salters.

sentences.zh: 由是鹽課大殖。

translations.literal: From this, salt revenue greatly increased.
translations.idiomatic: Salt revenues thereafter rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 浙江當造海船五十艘，下忱計度。

translations.literal: Zhejiang was to build fifty seagoing ships; the matter was sent down to Chen for planning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang was ordered to build fifty seagoing vessels, and Chen was asked to estimate the cost.

sentences.zh: 忱召問都匠，言一艘須米千石。

translations.literal: Chen summoned and asked the chief artisan, who said one ship required one thousand shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Chen consulted the chief shipwright, who said each vessel would require a thousand shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 忱以成大事不宜惜費，第減二十石，奏於朝，竟得報可。

translations.literal: Chen held that great undertakings should not stint on expense; he only reduced twenty shi, memorialized to court, and in the end received approval.
translations.idiomatic: Chen argued that great projects should not be penny-pinched; he trimmed only twenty shi per ship, submitted the plan, and won approval.

sentences.zh: 以九載秩滿，進左侍郎。

translations.literal: Having served nine years and his term fulfilled, he was promoted to Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years in office he was promoted to left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 六年命兼理湖州、嘉興二府稅糧，又命同刑科都給事中郭瑾錄南京刑獄。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was ordered also to manage tax grain in Huzhou and Jiaxing two prefectures, and also ordered together with Chief Supervising Secretary Guo Jin of the Punishments Bureau to review Nanjing criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was also put in charge of tax grain in Huzhou and Jiaxing and, with Chief Supervising Secretary Guo Jin of the Bureau of Punishments, assigned to review Nanjing criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 忱素樂易。

translations.literal: Chen was by nature easygoing.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was naturally easygoing.

sentences.zh: 先是，大理卿胡槩為巡撫，用法嚴。

translations.literal: Earlier, Censor-in-chief Hu Gai as pacification commissioner applied the law strictly.
translations.idiomatic: His predecessor Hu Gai, as censor-in-chief and pacification commissioner, had governed with strict law.

sentences.zh: 忱一切治以簡易，告訐者輒不省。

translations.literal: Chen governed everything with simplicity and ease; those who brought accusations he routinely ignored.
translations.idiomatic: Chen governed with light touch and simplicity, routinely ignoring accusers.

sentences.zh: 或面訐忱：「公不及胡公。」

translations.literal: Someone confronted Chen to his face: "You are not the equal of Lord Hu."
translations.idiomatic: Someone confronted him: "You are not the equal of Lord Hu."

sentences.zh: 忱笑曰：「胡卿敕旨，在祛除民害；

translations.literal: Chen smiled and said: "Lord Hu's imperial commission was to remove harm to the people;
translations.idiomatic: Chen smiled and said, "Lord Hu's commission was to remove harm to the people;

sentences.zh: 朝廷命我，但雲安撫軍民。

translations.literal: the court ordered me only to pacify troops and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: the court ordered me merely to pacify troops and civilians.

sentences.zh: 委寄正不同耳。」

translations.literal: The charge entrusted is plainly different."
translations.idiomatic: Our charges were plainly different."

sentences.zh: 既久任江南，與吏民相習若家人父子。

translations.literal: Having long served in Jiangnan, he was as familiar with clerks and people as family between father and son.
translations.idiomatic: Having long served in Jiangnan, he was as familiar with officials and commoners as a father with his sons.

sentences.zh: 每行村落，屏去騶從，與農夫餉婦相對，從容問所疾苦，為之商略處置。

translations.literal: Whenever he traveled to villages, he dismissed his runners and attendants, sat facing farmers and supplying wives, leisurely asking their hardships, and deliberated how to handle them.
translations.idiomatic: On village visits he dismissed his escort, sat with farmers and their wives, calmly asked their grievances, and worked out remedies.

sentences.zh: 其馭下也，雖卑官冗吏，悉開心訪納。

translations.literal: In governing subordinates, even low officials and trivial clerks, he wholeheartedly sought and received their counsel.
translations.idiomatic: With subordinates—even the lowliest clerks—he welcomed their counsel openly.

sentences.zh: 遇長吏有能，如況鍾及松江知府趙豫、常州知府莫愚、同知趙泰輩，則推心與咨畫，務盡其長，故事無不舉。

translations.literal: When he encountered capable senior officials, such as Kuang Zhong and Songjiang Prefect Zhao Yu, Changzhou Prefect Mo Yu, Vice Prefect Zhao Tai and the like, he opened his heart to consult with them, striving to bring out their strengths, so nothing under his charge went undone.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he met capable senior officials—Kuang Zhong, Songjiang Prefect Zhao Yu, Changzhou Prefect Mo Yu, Vice Prefect Zhao Tai, and others like them—he confided in them fully and drew on their strengths, so that nothing under his administration was left unfinished.

sentences.zh: 常詣松江相視水利，見嘉定、上海間，沿江生茂草，多淤流，乃浚其上流，使昆山、顧浦諸所水迅流駛下，壅遂盡滌。

translations.literal: He often went to Songjiang to inspect waterworks. Between Jiading and Shanghai he saw lush grass growing along the riverbanks with much silted flow. He dredged the upper reaches so that water from places such as Kunshan and Gupu rushed swiftly downstream, and the blockages were entirely washed away.
translations.idiomatic: He often traveled to Songjiang to inspect water control. Between Jiading and Shanghai he found thick riverside growth and heavy silting, so he dredged the upper reaches to send water from Kunshan, Gupu, and other points rushing downstream until every obstruction was cleared.

sentences.zh: 暇時以匹馬往來江上，見者不知其為巡撫也。

translations.literal: In his spare time he traveled up and down the river on a single horse; those who saw him did not know he was the pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In his leisure he rode a single horse up and down the river, and those who saw him had no idea he was the pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 歷宣德、正統二十年間，朝廷委任益專。

translations.literal: Over twenty years spanning the Xuande and Zhengtong reigns, the court's trust in him grew ever more exclusive.
translations.idiomatic: Across twenty years of the Xuande and Zhengtong reigns, the court's reliance on him grew ever more complete.

sentences.zh: 兩遭親喪，皆起復視事。

translations.literal: Twice he suffered the death of a parent; each time he was recalled from mourning to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he lost a parent, and each time he was recalled from mourning to resume his duties.

sentences.zh: 忱以此益發舒，見利害必言，言無不聽。

translations.literal: Chen thereby spoke out more freely; whenever he saw benefit or harm he spoke up, and nothing he said went unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: Chen took this as license to speak more boldly: whenever he saw benefit or harm he said so, and the court always listened.

sentences.zh: 初，欲減松江官田額，依民田起科。

translations.literal: At first he wished to reduce the quota for official land in Songjiang and assess it like commoner land.
translations.idiomatic: At first he proposed cutting Songjiang's official-land quota and assessing it at the same rate as private holdings.

sentences.zh: 戶部郭資、胡濙奏其變亂成法，請罪之，宣宗切責資等。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Guo Zi and Hu Ying memorialized that he was overturning established law and asked that he be punished; the Xuandzong Emperor sharply rebuked Guo and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue ministers Guo Zi and Hu Ying accused him of overturning established law and asked that he be punished; the Xuandzong Emperor sharply rebuked them instead.

sentences.zh: 忱嘗言：「吳淞江畔有沙塗柴場百五十頃，水草茂盛，蟲蜢多生其中。

translations.literal: Chen once said: "On the bank of the Wusong River there are one hundred fifty qing of sand-flats and firewood fields where grass and water flourish and locusts breed in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Chen once said, "On the Wusong River there are one hundred fifty qing of sand flats and brushland where grass and water are abundant and locusts breed in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 請募民開墾，可以足國課，消蟲災。」

translations.literal: Let us recruit people to open them for cultivation; this can meet state revenue and eliminate locust disasters."
translations.idiomatic: Recruit people to reclaim them, and we can meet state revenue needs while averting locust plagues."

sentences.zh: 又言：「丹徒、丹陽二縣田沒入江者，賦尚未除。

translations.literal: He also said: "In Dantu and Danyang two counties, land submerged in the river still has tax not yet remitted.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "In Dantu and Danyang, fields lost to the river still carry tax obligations that have never been lifted.

sentences.zh: 國初蠲稅之家，其田多並於富室，宜征其租，沒於江者除之，則額不虧而貧富均。

translations.literal: Households whose taxes were remitted at the dynasty's founding—their fields mostly merged into rich families' holdings. The rent from those should be collected, while fields lost to the river should be exempted; then the quota would not fall short and rich and poor would be balanced.
translations.idiomatic: Fields whose taxes were remitted at the founding of the dynasty have mostly been absorbed by wealthy households; those rents should be collected again, while submerged land should be exempted. Then the quota would hold and rich and poor would share the burden fairly.

sentences.zh: 無錫官田賦白米太重，請改征租米。」

translations.literal: Wuxi's tax on official land in white rice is too heavy; please convert it to assessed rent grain."
translations.idiomatic: Wuxi's official-land levy in polished white rice is too heavy; please convert it to rent grain instead."

sentences.zh: 悉報可。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 其因災荒請蠲貸，及所陳他利病無算。

translations.literal: His petitions for remission and loans during famines, and the other benefits and harms he stated, were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: His petitions for tax relief and grain loans in times of famine, and the other reforms and abuses he raised, were beyond number.

sentences.zh: 小者用便宜行之，無所顧慮。

translations.literal: Minor matters he handled by expedient authority without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Smaller matters he carried out on his own authority without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 久之見財賦充溢，益務廣大。

translations.literal: After long seeing revenues overflow, he pursued ever grander projects.
translations.idiomatic: As revenues swelled over time, he turned to ever grander undertakings.

sentences.zh: 修葺廨舍學校、先賢祠墓、橋梁道路，及崇飾寺觀，贈遺中朝官，資餉過客，無稍吝惜。

translations.literal: Repairing government offices, schools, shrines to sages, tombs, bridges and roads, and embellishing temples; gifting court officials, entertaining travelers—he never stinted in the least.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired government offices, schools, shrines to sages, tombs, bridges, and roads; adorned temples and monasteries; sent gifts to capital officials and provisioned traveling guests—never sparing expense.

sentences.zh: 胥吏漁蠹其中，亦不甚訾省。

translations.literal: Clerks preyed on these arrangements, yet he did not much scrutinize them.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks fattened themselves on these expenditures, yet he did little to check them.

sentences.zh: 以故屢召人言。

translations.literal: For this reason he was repeatedly summoned to answer accusations.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was repeatedly called to account.

sentences.zh: 九年，給事中李素等劾忱妄意變更，專擅科斂。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Supervising Secretary Li Su and others impeached Chen for presumptuously changing policy and levying taxes on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Supervising Secretary Li Su and others impeached Chen for unauthorized policy changes and arbitrary tax levies.

sentences.zh: 忱上章自訴。

translations.literal: Chen submitted a memorial in his own defense.
translations.idiomatic: Chen answered with a memorial pleading his own case.

sentences.zh: 帝以余米既為公用，置不問。

translations.literal: The emperor, since the surplus grain had already served public use, let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that the surplus grain had already served the public good and took no further action.

sentences.zh: 先是，奸民尹崇禮欲撓忱法，奏忱不當多征耗米，請究問倉庫主者，忱因罷前法。

translations.literal: Earlier, the wicked commoner Yin Chongli had wished to obstruct Chen's methods and memorialized that Chen should not levy so much surplus grain, asking that the granary keepers be investigated. Chen therefore abolished the earlier method.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the schemer Yin Chongli had tried to undermine Chen's system, accusing him of levying too much surplus grain and demanding an inquiry into the granary keepers. Chen then abolished his earlier method.

sentences.zh: 既而兩稅復逋，民無所賴，鹹稱不便。

translations.literal: Before long the two taxes again fell into arrears; the people had nothing to rely on and all said the change was inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the land tax fell into arrears again, the people had nothing to fall back on, and all complained that the change had made things worse.

sentences.zh: 忱乃奏按崇禮罪，舉行前法如故。

translations.literal: Chen then memorialized to punish Chongli according to law and restored the former method as before.
translations.idiomatic: Chen then memorialized to punish Chongli by law and restored his former system.

sentences.zh: 再以九載滿，進戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Again when nine years' tenure was complete, he was promoted to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When another nine-year term was complete, he was promoted to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 尋以江西人不得官戶部，乃改工部，仍巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon, because Jiangxi men could not hold the Revenue post, he was moved to the Ministry of Works while continuing as pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, because men from Jiangxi could not serve as revenue minister, he was transferred to the Ministry of Works while retaining his post as pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 然當時言理財者，無出忱右。

translations.literal: Yet among those who spoke of managing finances at the time, none surpassed Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet among those who managed state finances at the time, none surpassed Chen.

sentences.zh: 其治以愛民為本。

translations.literal: His governance took cherishing the people as its root.
translations.idiomatic: His governing principle was to put the people's welfare first.

sentences.zh: 濟農倉之設也，雖與民為期約，至時多不追取。

translations.literal: When the Farm Relief Granary was established, though deadlines were set with the people, when the time came he often did not pursue collection.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Farm Relief Granary set repayment deadlines with borrowers, when the time came Chen often did not press for collection.

sentences.zh: 每歲征收畢，逾正月中旬，輒下檄放糧，曰：「此百姓納與朝廷剩數，今還與百姓用之，努力種朝廷田，秋間又納朝廷稅也。」

translations.literal: Each year after collection was finished, past the middle of the first month, he would issue an order releasing grain, saying: "This is surplus the people paid to the court; now it is returned for the people's use. Work hard at planting the court's fields, and in autumn pay the court's tax again."
translations.idiomatic: Each year after the harvest levy was complete, past mid-first month he would issue an order releasing grain, saying, "This is surplus grain the people paid the court; now it is returned for your use. Work hard at planting the court's fields, and in autumn pay the court's tax again."

sentences.zh: 其所弛張變通，皆可為後法。

translations.literal: His adaptations and flexibilities could all serve as models for later ages.
translations.idiomatic: His flexible adaptations could all serve as models for later generations.

sentences.zh: 諸府余米，數多至不可校，公私饒足，施及外郡。

translations.literal: Surplus grain in the prefectures was so great it could not be counted; public and private stores were abundant, and benefits spread to other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus grain in the prefectures grew so vast it was beyond counting; public and private stores overflowed, and the benefits reached neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，江北大饑，都御史王竑從忱貸米三萬石。

translations.literal: Early in the Jingtai reign, northern Jiang suffered great famine; Censor-in-chief Wang Gong borrowed thirty thousand shi of grain from Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingtai reign, when northern Jiang suffered severe famine, Censor-in-chief Wang Gong borrowed thirty thousand shi of grain from Chen.

sentences.zh: 忱為計至來年麥熟，以十萬石畀之。

translations.literal: Chen calculated through to the next year's wheat harvest and allotted one hundred thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen calculated needs through the next wheat harvest and gave him one hundred thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 性機警。

translations.literal: By nature he was alert and clever.
translations.idiomatic: He was quick-witted by nature.

sentences.zh: 錢谷鉅萬，一屈指無遺算。

translations.literal: Revenue figures in the tens of thousands—one flick of his fingers and none was missed.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue figures in the tens of thousands—he could tally them at a glance without missing a single item.

sentences.zh: 嘗陰為冊記陰晴風雨。

translations.literal: He secretly kept a register of clear and cloudy, windy and rainy days.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly kept a daily record of sun, cloud, wind, and rain.

sentences.zh: 或言某日江中遇風失米，忱言是日江中無風，其人驚服。

translations.literal: Someone said that on a certain day wind on the river lost grain; Chen said there was no wind on the river that day, and the man was astonished and convinced.
translations.idiomatic: When someone claimed that grain had been lost to wind on the river on a certain day, Chen said there had been no wind on the river that day, and the man was astonished into submission.

sentences.zh: 有奸民故亂其舊案嘗之。

translations.literal: A wicked commoner once deliberately scrambled his old records to test him.
translations.idiomatic: Once a schemer deliberately scrambled his old case records to test him.

sentences.zh: 忱曰：「汝以某時就我決事，我為汝斷理，敢相紿耶？」

translations.literal: Chen said: "You came to me for judgment at such-and-such a time; I decided your case for you—how dare you try to deceive me?"
translations.idiomatic: Chen said, "You came to me for judgment at such-and-such a time, and I ruled on your case—how dare you try to deceive me?"

sentences.zh: 三殿重建，詔征牛膠萬斤，為彩繪用。

translations.literal: Reconstruction of the Three Halls—an edict levied ten thousand jin of ox hide glue for painted decoration.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Halls were rebuilt, an edict levied ten thousand jin of ox-hide glue for painted decoration.

sentences.zh: 忱適赴京，言庫貯牛皮，歲久朽腐，請出煎膠，俟歸市皮償庫。

translations.literal: Chen happened to be at court and said the storehouse held ox hides long rotted; he asked to boil them for glue and buy hides to repay the store on his return.
translations.idiomatic: Chen happened to be at court and said the storehouse held ox hides long since rotted; he asked permission to boil them for glue and buy fresh hides to repay the store on his return.

sentences.zh: 土木之變，當國者議，欲焚通州倉，絕寇資。

translations.literal: At the Tumu crisis, those in charge debated burning the Tongzhou granary to deny the enemy supplies.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tumu crisis, those in charge debated burning the Tongzhou granary to deny the enemy supplies.

sentences.zh: 忱適議事至，言倉米數百萬，可充京軍一歲餉，令自往取，則立盡，何至遂付煨燼。

translations.literal: Chen happened to arrive for deliberation and said the granary held millions of shi of grain, enough for the capital garrison's year's rations—order them to come take it themselves and it would be gone at once; why throw it all to the flames?
translations.idiomatic: Chen arrived just then for deliberations and said the granary held millions of shi—enough for the capital garrison's year's rations. Order the troops to come and take it themselves, and it would be gone at once. Why consign it all to the flames?

sentences.zh: 頃之，詔趣造盔甲數百萬。

translations.literal: Before long an edict urgently ordered several million suits of armor.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward an edict urgently commanded the manufacture of several million suits of armor.

sentences.zh: 忱計明盔浴鐵工多，令且沃錫，數日畢辦。

translations.literal: Chen reckoned that bright-helmet bath-iron workers were many; he ordered tin to be poured over them for now, and within days the task was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Chen noted that tin-plated helmet smiths were plentiful and ordered temporary tin plating; within days the order was filled.

sentences.zh: 忱既被劾，帝命李敏代之，敕無輕易忱法。

translations.literal: After Chen was impeached, the emperor ordered Li Min to replace him and instructed that Chen's methods not be lightly changed.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen was impeached, the emperor appointed Li Min in his place and ordered that Chen's methods not be lightly altered.

sentences.zh: 然自是戶部括所積余米為公賦，儲備蕭然。

translations.literal: Yet from then on the Ministry of Revenue seized accumulated surplus grain as public revenue, and reserves were depleted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from then on the Ministry of Revenue swept accumulated surplus grain into public revenue, and reserves were soon exhausted.

sentences.zh: 其後吳大饑，道堇相望，課逋如故矣。

translations.literal: Later Wu suffered great famine; corpses lined the roads yet tax arrears continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wu suffered great famine and corpses lined the roads, tax arrears continued as before.

sentences.zh: 民益思忱不已，即生祠處處祀之。

translations.literal: The people missed Chen ever more; living shrines were erected everywhere to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: The people missed Chen ever more fondly, and living shrines sprang up everywhere to honor him.

sentences.zh: 景泰四年十月卒。

translations.literal: He died in the tenth month of the fourth year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of Jingtai 4.

sentences.zh: 謚文襄。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 況鍾等自有傳。

translations.literal: Kuang Zhong and the others have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang Zhong and the others have biographies of their own.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：宋禮、陳瑄治河通運道，為國家經久計，生民被澤無窮。

translations.literal: Commentary: Song Li and Chen Xuan managed the rivers and opened transport routes—a long-term plan for the state; the living people have received their benefit without end.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Song Li and Chen Xuan dredged the rivers and opened transport routes as a lasting plan for the state, and the people have reaped their bounty without end.

sentences.zh: 周忱治財賦，民不擾而廩有余羨。

translations.literal: Zhou Chen managed revenues: the people were undisturbed yet the granaries overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chen managed the revenues so that the people were unburdened and the granaries brimmed with surplus.

sentences.zh: 此無他故，殫公心以體國，而才力足以濟之。

translations.literal: There is no other reason: they devoted their public hearts to serving the state, and their talent and strength were equal to the task.
translations.idiomatic: There was no other secret: they gave their whole public hearts to the state, and their talent and strength were equal to the work.

sentences.zh: 誠異夫造端興事，僥一時之功，智籠巧取，為科斂之術者也。

translations.literal: Truly they differ from those who initiate projects hoping for momentary success, who with clever cunning harvest gains as a technique of extortion.
translations.idiomatic: They were truly unlike those who launch projects to seize a moment's glory, who with clever schemes and artful extraction turn governance into extortion.

sentences.zh: 然河渠之利，世享其成，而忱之良法美意，未幾而澌滅無余，民用重困。

translations.literal: Yet the benefit of rivers and canals generations enjoy to completion, while Chen's fine laws and benevolent intentions vanished within little time without remainder, and the people's use grew heavily burdened.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the benefit of rivers and canals endures for generations, while Chen's fine laws and benevolent designs vanished within little time without a trace, and the people were burdened anew.

sentences.zh: 豈非成功之有跡者易以循，而用法之因人者難其繼哉。

translations.literal: Is it not that achievements with visible traces are easy to follow, while methods that depend on the man are hard to continue?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not that achievements with visible traces are easy to follow, while methods that live in the man himself are hard to carry on?

sentences.zh: 雖然，見小利而樂紛更，不能不為當日之嘵嘵者惜也。

translations.literal: Even so, those who saw small gains and delighted in ceaseless change—we must regret the clamorers of that day.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, those who saw small gains and delighted in endless change—we must mourn the noisy faultfinders of that day.
